name: Levonorgestrel IUD
summary: Among the most effective options and the one that most reliably lightens or stops periods. Insertion is uncomfortable, and it takes a clinician to put in and to take out.

name: Copper IUD
summary: Hormone-free and the most effective emergency contraception if placed within five days. Periods usually get heavier and crampier, especially the first year.

name: Etonogestrel implant
summary: A rod under the skin of the upper arm. As effective as an IUD without a pelvic procedure. Bleeding becomes unpredictable, which is the usual reason people ask for removal.

name: Progestin injection
summary: Nothing to think about between visits and completely undetectable. Fertility can take months to return, and bone density falls while on it.

name: Combined pill
summary: The generic estrogen-plus-progestin pill. Predictable cycles and real benefits for acne and cramps, but it has to be taken every day. Switch to the pills view to compare formulations.

name: Progestin-only pill
summary: The estrogen-free daily pill, usable when estrogen is off the table. Timing matters more than with a combined pill, and bleeding is less predictable.

name: Contraceptive patch
summary: Weekly instead of daily. It is visible on the skin, and it may work less well at a BMI over 30.

name: Vaginal ring
summary: Placed and removed by the user, once a month. Annovera lasts a full year. A partner may be able to feel it.

name: External condom
summary: The only method here that also prevents sexually transmitted infection, which is why it is often used alongside something else rather than instead of it.

name: Internal condom
summary: Also prevents infection, and can be inserted ahead of time. Less effective at preventing pregnancy than an external condom and harder to find.

name: Diaphragm with spermicide
summary: Hormone-free and reusable, inserted before sex. Needs a prescription and raises the risk of urinary tract infection.

name: Vaginal gel
summary: Hormone-free and used only when needed. The least effective prescription option, and expensive without coverage.

name: Spermicide or sponge
summary: Available off the shelf and hormone-free, but the failure rate is high enough that it works best paired with something else.

name: Fertility awareness
summary: No devices, no hormones, nothing to obtain. It requires regular cycles, daily tracking, and abstaining or using a barrier on fertile days.

name: Withdrawal
summary: Free and always available. It depends entirely on a cooperative partner and about one in four people using it get pregnant in a year.

name: Tubal ligation
summary: Permanent and highly effective. Requires anesthesia and up to two weeks of recovery, and it should be treated as irreversible.

name: Vasectomy
summary: Simpler, cheaper, and safer than tubal ligation, with about two days of recovery. Also permanent. Requires a partner willing to have it done.

name: Levonorgestrel-ethinyl estradiol 0.1/20
summary: A reasonable default. The lowest common estrogen dose, which means fewer estrogen side effects and a bit more spotting in the first few months.

name: Norgestimate-ethinyl estradiol 0.25/35
summary: The other common opener. The higher estrogen dose gives steadier cycle control than a 20 mcg pill, and norgestimate carries an FDA acne indication.

name: Norethindrone acetate-ethinyl estradiol 1/20
summary: Only four hormone-free days instead of seven, which suppresses the ovaries more completely and cuts the headaches and mood dips that cluster in the placebo week.

name: Drospirenone-ethinyl estradiol 3/0.02
summary: The only pill approved for premenstrual dysphoric disorder. Drospirenone spares potassium, so check a level if the person takes anything else that raises it.

name: Drospirenone-ethinyl estradiol 3/0.03
summary: The 21/7 version of Yaz at a higher estrogen dose. Better cycle control, more placebo-week symptoms.

name: Norgestimate-ethinyl estradiol triphasic
dose: Doses step up across the pack
summary: No proven advantage over a monophasic pill. The pills must be taken in order and the pack cannot be run continuously.

name: Levonorgestrel-ethinyl estradiol 84/7
summary: Four withdrawal bleeds a year instead of thirteen. Expect more spotting for the first few months, settling by about six.

name: Levonorgestrel-ethinyl estradiol 90/20
summary: No placebo week at all, and usually no periods. Unscheduled spotting is common for the first three to six months, then settles.

name: Estradiol valerate-dienogest
summary: Uses estradiol rather than ethinyl estradiol, which appears gentler on clotting factors and lipids. Four-phase dosing, nine days of backup at start, and no generic.

name: Estetrol-drospirenone
summary: A newer estrogen with less effect on liver clotting proteins in short studies. No long-term outcome data and no generic.

name: Norethindrone 0.35 mg
summary: Estrogen-free, so it works with a clot history, migraine with aura, or hypertension. It has to land in the same three-hour window every day, and about half of users still ovulate.

name: Drospirenone 4 mg
summary: Estrogen-free but suppresses ovulation like a combined pill, and forgives a dose up to 24 hours late. No generic, and watch potassium.

name: Norgestrel 0.075 mg
summary: The only pill sold over the counter in the US. No prescription, no exam, no blood pressure check. Estrogen-free, taken at the same time daily.
